heart-location.def: Your heart sits in the mediastinum, between the lungs, behind the sternum and on the diaphragm, with about two thirds of its mass left of the midline. Its apex is the pointed lower tip, at about the fifth intercostal space on the left; its base is the broad upper, back end where the large vessels attach.

pericardium.def: The covering around the heart: a tough outer fibrous pericardium of dense connective tissue, and an inner serous pericardium folded into a parietal layer and a visceral layer with a film of serous fluid (the pericardial cavity) between them. The fibrous layer plus the parietal layer form the pericardial sac.

heart-wall.def: The three layers of the heart wall: the epicardium on the outside (the same layer as the visceral pericardium), the thick myocardium of cardiac muscle in the middle, and the endocardium, an endothelial lining, on the inside.

cardiac-tamponade.def: Compression of the heart by blood or fluid collecting in the pericardial cavity. Because the fibrous pericardium cannot stretch quickly, pressure in the sac rises, the heart cannot fill between beats, and blood pressure falls.

chambers.def: The four spaces inside the heart: two upper atria that receive blood from veins and two lower ventricles that pump blood into arteries. Surface grooves (the coronary and interventricular sulci) mark their boundaries; auricles, pectinate muscles and trabeculae carneae are features of their walls.

great-vessels.def: The large vessels at the base of the heart: the superior and inferior venae cavae (into the right atrium), the pulmonary trunk (out of the right ventricle, splitting into the right and left pulmonary arteries), the pulmonary veins (into the left atrium) and the aorta (out of the left ventricle, rising as the ascending aorta and curving over as the aortic arch).
